articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metasurfaces for Index Modulation in 5G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recent research on index modulation (IM) techniques shows great promise in improving the energy and spectral efficiencies of high data-rate 5G wireless communications. In this work, we introduce a reconfigurable software-defined metasurface to implement IM techniques in 5G transceivers. In particular, we define implementation of spatial and subcarrier index modulations using a reconfigurable metasurface antenna, including beam steering and phase modulation capabilities. We present a metasurface aperture that can modulate and multiplex communications signals over the spectral, spatial, and temporal domains using space-time coding of unit elements.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized GNSS Antenna for Satellite Platforms
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband circularly polarized antenna for GNSS applications. The antenna consists of four triangular patches excited with 90° phase differences in between to generate right-hand circular polarization. The antenna operating frequency cover the whole GNSS band 1.164-1.610 GHz. The antenna is also modified to incorporate a cavity for LNA placement. The axial ratio and gain measurements indicate a good agreement with the simulations. The antenna presents a compact yet effective GNSS antenna solution for satellite platforms.

articleTitle: Overview of Electronic Attacks Against Passive Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Passive radars (PR) are becoming more popular in both commercial and research environments. If, as they are expected to, become deployed in military surveillance applications, their vulnerability to electronic attacks (EA) needs to be thoroughly investigated. This paper presents aspects of countering FM, DAB and DVB- T based PR systems using various attack strategies. The effects of various jamming waveforms are investigated. It is shown that under certain conditions, successful EA can be achieved with relatively low power. We demonstrate the importance of a direct signal canceller which causes a FM based PR system to be more tolerant to jamming when the reference and surveillance antennas are co-located as opposed to being separated.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Omnidirectional UHF RFID Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: UHF RFID reader antennas are often patches operating in the fundamental mode, with broadside radiation patterns. For some applications, it is convenient to have planar antennas with omni-directional patterns, which can have greater angular coverage than conventional reader antennas. A circular-patch antenna operating in a monopole mode is presented. Using both shorting pins and slots, the antenna is highly miniaturized. The effect of different antenna tuning parameters are presented, and their trade-offs are considered. An optimized design is presented and its properties are discussed.

articleTitle: Improved Efficiency and Accuracy Using Duality in Hybrid SIBC-BEM Formulation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The paper presents a hybrid formulation coupling the surface impedance boundary condition, to deal with conductive and magnetic materials, and the boundary element method to account rigorously for the regularity conditions of the magnetic field at infinity. Based on duality relations, the field variables are associated to spatial elements starting from the dual mesh, overcoming some of the performance issues of the previously published results. The new formulation is suitable to be used to study wireless power transfer devices for automotive applications.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of Starting Performance of Induction Motors with Non-Skewed Asymmetric Rotor Bars
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Non-skewed asymmetric rotor bars can be used to replace the skewed rotors for eliminating the slot harmonic field and weaken the noise and vibration of effectively in cage induction motors. However, due to the complex spatial distribution of rotor bars, the starting performance may be affected by the modulated air-gap flux density. This paper studies the starting performances of a 5.5-kW, 4-pole induction motor, such as the starting current, the starting torque and the maximum torque, by using Finite Element Method (FEM). Prototpes of 5.5 kW induction motor with asymmetric rotor bars are manufactured and experiment validations are also performed.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Volume-Volume (6-D) Integrals for Numerical Evaluation by Double Application of the Divergence Theorem
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In the present paper, we propose the application of the surface divergence theorem for the integration of double volumetric integrals for both source and test domain of the 6-D reaction integrals. The resulting 6-D volume integrals are expressed as two radial integrals plus two surface integrals over the source and observation domain boundaries. The radial integrations in the physical domain should be well-behaved and easily performed for arbitrary polyhedral domains. The method is numerically validated for static and dynamic kernels arising in the Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE), i.e., for kernels with 1/R singularities, and linear basis functions.

articleTitle: Automated CAD and Modeling of Origami Structures for Reconfigurable Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) simulation of origami-inspired antenna structures has been a challenge due to its complex and sometimes counter-intuitive 3-D designs. In this work, we show the development of a unified automated tool that constructs the CAD models for origami type structures for conducting full-wave simulations. In the proposed toolset, we have used the well known Mathematica Notebook called `Tessellatica', for obtaining origami geometries and subsequently generated CAD models for full-wave simulations in ANSYS High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). The developed toolset can be used to build HFSS 3-D models and conduct full-wave simulations for an arbitrary origami type structure.

articleTitle: Metasurface Design Using Level-Set and Gradient Descent Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Optical dielectric metasurfaces are typically composed of meta-atoms in the form of simple parametrized geometrical shapes. Meta-atoms with more complex cross-sectional geometries may enable better performance and multiple functionalities. Here we present a metasurface design technique based on a combination of the level-set method and the adjoint optimization technique that efficiently explores the available degrees of freedom of meta-atoms. As a proof of concept, we design a 75° metasurface beam deflector with 80% deflection efficiency.

articleTitle: Proximity Effect of UWB U-Slot Patch Antenna on Human Body
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the proximity effect of Ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna on human body is considered and demonstrated. A U-Slot loaded planar UWB antenna is designed on TMM3 (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=3.27) using single layer circuit board technology. The antenna has shown 75% impedance bandwidth in free space. A human body model having three layers (skin, fat and muscle) is developed. The effect of the human body on the antenna performance is analyzed and characterized in terms of the reflection-coefficient and specific absorption rate (SAR). The effect of the antenna-body is analyzed for off body applications. The UWB U-Slot antenna exhibits low SAR while maintaining reasonable impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: Single Layer Vivaldi Antenna Feed Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: For many applications tapered slot antennas are attractive with broad bandwidth, medium gain and good pattern stability. Many designs can be found in the literature but the exponentially tapered slot (i.e., Vivaldi aerial) has good performance. The frequencies of interest are 8 to 10 GHz where planar antenna designs are considered for ease of fabrication and integration. A single layer planar Vivaldi tapered slot-type antenna is simulated and fabricated to investigate the simplest way to feed such antennas without limiting performance. The results show that a SMA connector from the rear and soldered on the front can be used but requires an air gap so the SMA does not touch the substrate. This paper summarizes a numerical investigation using FEKO to provide feed alternatives. The results serve to guide the selection of antenna elements and unbalanced feed arrangements for RF system developers.

articleTitle: Space Fence Radar Overview
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The AN/FSY-3 Space Fence Radar, located on Kwajalein Atoll, is a ground-based S-band radar integrated with an Operations Center designed to greatly enhance the Air Force Space Surveillance Network. Space Fence will revolutionize Space Situational Awareness using advanced phased array radar technology. Space Fence will provide catalog completeness, accuracy and timeliness with vastly improved performance in Low Earth Orbit and capability to support missions in Geosynchronous Earth Orbit. Modeling & Simulation has played a key role in all phases of the Space Fence radar program. In addition, Modeling & Simulation will play an important role in the formal Government testing of requirements that depend on simulated environments or unique orbital events.

articleTitle: A Multi-Transmitter Configuration for High-Safety Wireless Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A multi-transmitter configuration made by an array of passive resonant elements placed in the proximity of the driver coil for inductive Wireless Power Transfer applications is presented. The array is able to significantly decrease the electric field level produced by the fed loop at the operative frequency of 6 MHz, thus reducing the potentially dangerous radiation over biological tissues (i.e., the Specific Absorption Rate, SAR). Nonetheless, the proposed arrangement preserves the same efficiency level of the simple driver-receiver system and it does not affect the useful working distance. Electromagnetic simulations have been performed to evaluate the SAR reduction and the efficiency levels achieved by the multi-transmitter configuration in comparison with the driver-receiver system. The proposed solution can be extremely useful in all the WPT applications in which the SAR exposure is a concern, such as automotive applications, biomedical implants and rechargeable devices.

articleTitle: Fast Algorithm of Arbitrary Beam Propagation Based on Adaptive Elliptical Gaussian Beam Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An algorithm for arbitrary electromagnetic (EM) beam propagation is proposed and well demonstrated in this paper. The essential idea of this algorithm is to decompose arbitrary beam into a small number of elliptical Gaussian beams, which is similar but different from existing diffracted Gaussian beam analysis (DGBA) based on Gabor expansion. The proposed algorithm utilizing adaptive Gaussian beam matching method is much more efficient than regular decomposition strategy by Gabor expansion. Beam propagation is then calculated by these elliptical Gaussian beams' superposed analytical results, with accuracy comparable with physical optics (PO) theory. This fast algorithm can be suitable for analyzing beam propagation in electrically-large systems, such as reflector antennas and quasi-optical (QO) transforming systems.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Origami Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Reconfigurable, tunable, multifunctional, deployable, and UWB high-performance antenna systems are expected to play a significant role in next generation communication, reconnaissance, sensing and energy harvesting airborne and spaceborne systems. Towards this goal, in recent years, significant advances have been made in: 1) antenna miniaturization, 2) ultra-wideband (UWB) antennas with as much as 10:1 bandwidth or larger, 3) antenna reconfiguration using MEMS and phase-change material (PCM) switches, 4) conductive textiles for flexible antennas, 5) conductive inks and flexible materials, and 7) smart materials for actuation and sensing. However, to date, adaptable, foldable and deployable electromagnetic structures that can physically self-morph to modify antenna and RF circuit performance for multifunctionality, have yet to be explored in a reliable manner. Recently, origami folding techniques have been used to develop new types of reconfigurable antennas, thereby creating a new class of EM structures The scope of this paper is to give a brief review analysis on the field of origami inspired EM radiating structures, by presenting the past the present and the future of this newly born field.

articleTitle: Quantifying Subgridding Errors when Modeling Multiscale Structures with FDTD
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper discusses the growing subgridding errors in Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) analysis when applied on electrically large subgrids. FDTD simulations in 1D and 2D spaces are used with a 1:3 contrast ratio. Error levels are found to be linearly proportional to the subgrid's electrical dimension along the wave's propagation path. This linear growth suggests numerical phase error mismatch between coarse and fine grids as the subgridding error source.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metasurfaces for Index Modulation in 5G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recent research on index modulation (IM) techniques shows great promise in improving the energy and spectral efficiencies of high data-rate 5G wireless communications. In this work, we introduce a reconfigurable software-defined metasurface to implement IM techniques in 5G transceivers. In particular, we define implementation of spatial and subcarrier index modulations using a reconfigurable metasurface antenna, including beam steering and phase modulation capabilities. We present a metasurface aperture that can modulate and multiplex communications signals over the spectral, spatial, and temporal domains using space-time coding of unit elements.

articleTitle: Accelerating the FDTD Algorithm on CPUs with MATLAB's Parallel Computing Toolbox
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Investigating the improvement of MATLAB based finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulations using central processing units (CPUs) is the goal of this paper. The MATLAB parallel toolbox along with modern multi-core CPUs are used with no external dependencies or libraries and no expensive or complicated hardware acceleration units.

articleTitle: On Higher-Order Nyström Discretization of Scalar Potential Integral Equation for Penetrable Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A higher-order Nyström scheme is developed for discretizing the scalar potential integral equation (SPIE) for analyzing electromagnetic field/wave interactions on penetrable scatterers. The unknown scalar potential and its normal derivative are expanded using higher-order Lagrange interpolation functions. Inserting this expansion into the SPIE and point-testing the resulting equation yields a matrix system that is solved for the unknown expansion coefficients. Numerical results demonstrate that this matrix system is well-conditioned regardless of the discretization order and mesh density, and that its solution has higher-order convergence.

articleTitle: Overview of the Iterative Solver in HFSS for Analyzing Frequency Domain Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the iterative solver in ANSYS HFSS for solving large-scale problems obtained from the finite element analysis of time-harmonic Maxwell's Equations. To this end, Krylov subspace methods with effective preconditioning and parallelizable routines are presented to extend the applicability and efficiency of frequency domain solver. Several real-life examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy as well as efficiency of the iterative approach.

articleTitle: Suppressing E-Plane Scan Resonance for UWB Millimeter-Wave Differential Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recent advancements in differential Radio Frequency (RF) front-ends at millimeter-waves (mm-wave) create a need for high gain differentially fed arrays for 5G applications. In this paper, we present an ultra-wideband (UWB) mm-wave dual polarized Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) with a novel differential feeding network. Notably, we introduce a new H-Wall structure used to eliminate common-mode coupling that causes E-Plane scan resonances with high radiation efficiency and 45° scanning in both planes. This differential TCDA (D-TCDA) is developed for operation across K-Ka and 5G bands (viz. 22-80 GHz) in a low profile of 1.38 mm.

articleTitle: A Discontinuous Galerkin Framework for Multiphysics Simulation of Photoconductive Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A discontinuous Galerkin (DG) framework is developed for multiphysics simulation of plasmonic photoconductive devices. The nonequilibrium steady state is modeled by the coupled system of Poisson and drift-diffusion (DD) equations and this system is solved using a nonlinear DG scheme. The optical-to-terahertz (THz) conversion process is modeled by the coupled system of Maxwell and time dependent DD equations and this system is solved using a time domain DG scheme. Numerical experiments show that the proposed scheme provides accurate results.

articleTitle: On the Validity of Time Domain Methods for Complex Cavities
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This work evaluates the applicability of computational electromagnetic methods for simulating the response of a typical aircraft weapon bay. The goal is to develop a prediction of maximum expected electric field levels in the bay for evaluating EMC, including hazards of electromagnetic radiation to ordnance. A generalized geometry is created with traits similar to an aircraft bay. The Transmission Line Matrix method is used to simulate the response of the bay at 1830 MHz using a near field source in CST Microwave Studio. Results are evaluated for Chi-squared distribution with six degrees of freedom and the predicted number of modes.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Contour Integral on Curved Edges in Time Domain Equivalent Edge Currents
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The closed-form evaluation of the radiation integral in time domain physical theory of diffraction (PTD) equivalent edge currents (EECs) on quadratic edges of quadratic triangular surfaces, is presented. The radiation integral is interpreted as a Radon transform and the closed-form expressions are obtained by finding the intersection of the plane, which is formed by the propagation direction of the incident wave and the observation direction, and quadratic edge. A numerical example that shows the accuracy and validity of the scheme is presented.

articleTitle: Digital Metasurfaces Controlled by Light
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we will introduce a kind of remote-mode digital metasurfaces that are controlled by the illuminating light. By tuning the intensity of LED light, the digital coding metasurfaces enable dynamically reconfigurable radiation beams or tunable near-field distributions. Experimental demonstrations were carried out at microwave frequencies. The presented dynamical remote-tuning metasurfaces can be tuned in a non-contact remote fashion.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Magnetic Shielding of a Thin Conducting Screen Against a Small Loop
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The classical electromagnetic problem represented by a small loop axially parallel to a thin conductive planar shield of infinite extent is addressed in the time domain. The problem is solved analytically through a modified Cagniard-de Hoop approach and numerically through the double inverse Hankel/Fourier transform. Although some approximations are made, the analytical method is the most useful in predicting the main time-domain shielding characteristics.

articleTitle: Stochastic LIM for Transient Solution of Electromagnetic and Circuit Problems with Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Stochastic LIM was introduced for fast and accurate simulation of circuits with random elements. The method combines Latency Insertion Method with Stochastic Galerkin Method to formulate a finite difference-based transient circuit solver for simulation of circuits with uncertainties. The random nodal voltages and branch currents, along with the random circuit element values, are expanded using generalized Polynomial Chaos basis functions to form an augmented system which is solved using LIM. A sampling-based method proposed to calculate expansion coefficients as inputs to Stochastic LIM.

articleTitle: 2D Anistropic Media Based Metasurface Absorbing Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The metasurface absorbing boundary conditions (MS-ABC) using 2-D finite difference time domain (FDTD) technique for anisotropic media are presented in this paper. These ABC are synthesized using equivalent surface currents based on Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs). The anisotropic media constitutes of variable permittivity and conductivity in the x-y computational domain. Therefore, the simulated results are computed on all four metasurface boundary walls with metal cylinders terminated at these walls.

articleTitle: Design of Graded Dielectric Waveguides with Preferential Band-Pass Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A Neural-Network-biased Genetic Algorithm is employed to design all dielectric waveguide with periodic structures with preferential band-pass frequencies. Preliminary results indicate that an optimum periodic structure design exist for target frequency transmission and highlights the need for robust optimization scheme such as the one described here.

articleTitle: Origami-Tunable Frequency Selective Surfaces: A Design Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An origami design optimization framework is developed to predict fold topologies of frequency selective surfaces that are tuned through physical reconfiguration. The design methods combines electromagnetics and mechanics into a single tool for fold-based RF performance.

articleTitle: Radiated EM Flux Based Diagnostic Approach for Stator Insulation Failures in Inverter Fed Motors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Analysis of harmonics and inter-harmonics components in the spectrum of the radiated electromagnetic (EM) field is proposed for the detection of induction motor (IM) windings' insulation failure. The IM is fed through a voltage source inverter (VSI) operating under the classical direct torque controller (DTC). To investigate the EM spectrum, the radiated magnetic field intensity (→\pmbH) was calculated at an observer point in a physics-based finite element analysis (FEA) platform.

articleTitle: Large Waveguide Slotted Array with Shaped Patterns
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Genetic Algorithms(GAs) is employed to synthesis the large fan beam shaped pattern waveguide slotted array. Waveguide phase shifters are used to compensate the definite phases for each waveguide. The whole array is divided into eight partitions to broaden the bandwidth. Full wave simulations confirm the design of the shaped pattern antenna that will be used in the altimeter payload.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Colors and Memory with Al Metafilms
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We proposed an all-aluminum metasurface for dynamic optical displays and high-density data storage. The metasurface is composed of aluminum nanoantennae attached on aluminum back-reflector. When illuminated with broadband light, such metasurface reflects a broad palette of colors with a rotating polarizer and analyzer. Based on this feature, customized color sequences are created to enable high-density data storage. Also, another metasurface consisting of aluminum gap-plasmon-type centrosymmetric “i-shaped” dimmers is proposed. Full-color generation is theoretically achieved by adjusting the resonator dimensions and polarizer angle.

articleTitle: Comparison of Methods for Dielectric Characterization of Additively Manufactured Materials
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: As additive manufacturing (AM) gains traction in the field of antennas, characterizing the electromagnetic properties of AM materials becomes paramount for comparison to simulation and modeling. The Nicholson-Ross-Weir (NRW) and reference-plane invariant (RPI) methods are two well-known algorithms used for the extraction of complex permittivity from S-parameters of material samples measured in a waveguide. This paper gives a brief overview of the two methods and then compares the measured complex permittivity of various AM samples.

articleTitle: On Reduced-Cost Design Optimization of Antennas Using Trust-Region Gradient Search
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A reduced-cost gradient search with numerical derivatives for design optimization of antenna structures is presented. Our approach involves management of the antenna response Jacobians based on relative relocation of the design during subsequent algorithm iterations, as well as the size of the trust region (i.e., optimization domain at current iteration). Consistent computational savings are demonstrated (40 percent on average as compared to the reference algorithm) for a set of benchmark antennas, along the algorithm robustness.

articleTitle: Heating Characteristics of a Newly Developed RF Cavity Resonator for Hyperthermia that Targets Deep-Seated Tumor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We have numerically and experimentally investigated the heating characteristics of a newly developed RF cavity resonator for hyperthermia that targets deep-seated tumor. The new cavity resonator allows only the affected part to be inserted. From calculated and measured results, while the surface region in the phantom inside the cavity is heated to a high temperature, the deep region is heated to a slightly higher temperature. Although it is necessary to cool down the surface of the phantom by the water bolus, it is found that this applicator can heat the deep-seated tumor.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Textile Antenna with Omni-Directional Radiation for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel planar textile antenna with an omnidirectional radiation pattern is presented for wearable applications. The omnidirectional radiation is achieved by exciting four rotated open-ended slots with uniform amplitude and phase. The operating principles are explained with the help of equivalent circuit models and current distribution. The antenna is verified experimentally, showing good performance in terms of impedance bandwidth, omni-directional pattern, radiation efficiency and robustness to deformation and phantom loading.

articleTitle: Properties of the Conformal CSCMR System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, the evolution of Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) systems is presented. Such systems are highly efficient and misalignment insensitive. The design and miniaturization of these systems is presented here. The performance of CSCMR systems is validated using simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Calculation on Magnetostrictive Deformation of Motor Core Under the Non-Sinusoidal Excitation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The magnetostrictions in a non-oriented electrical steel sheets are an important cause of motor vibrations and noises. The presence of non-sinusoidal magnetic flux density brings about larger vibrations and noises. In this paper, a standard monolithic measurement system is employed to measure the magnetostriction in a non-oriented electrical steel sheet when a third harmonic is overlapped on a pure sinusoidal magnetic flux density. Based on the analysis of measured magnetostrictive property, a dynamic estimation model of magnetostrictive strain is proposed and verified. The results are helpful for further investigation of motor vibrations and noises.

articleTitle: Superformula - Inspired Split-Ring Resonators with Applications to Compact Bandpass Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We introduce an effective technique for miniaturizing a split-ring resonator (SRR) structure by replacing its conventional circular rings with shapes obtained from the superformula. By maintaining the resonator's effective electrical lengths and the gaps between the rings, our experiments have found it possible to achieve a comparable electrical performance at a reduced physical size. To validate the design concept, cross-like SRR bandpass filter (BPF) layouts with a 1.2 GHz center frequency are simulated and measured. A 21.3% reduction in the physical area is achieved with acceptable ports matching and transmission parameters.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Polynomial Chaos for Variation Analysis of Silicon Photonics Microresonators
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a polynomial chaos (PC) based numerical approach for the variation analysis of silicon photonics microresonators (MRs) in the presence of inevitable fabrication process variations. In particular, we develop low-dimensional component-level PC metamodels of standard quantities of interest which are then used to model the impact of fabrication process variations on the higher dimensional device-level quantities of interest. We demonstrate that the proposed indirect approach is much more computationally efficient when compared with the conventional approach of directly generating PC metamodels for device-level quantities of interest.

articleTitle: A Novel Mid-Infrared Metalens Using a Hyperbolic Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel metalens in the mid infrared range from 6.4um to 10um is designed. It consists of a plasmonic waveguide coupler (PWC), on a slab of type I hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) on the top of a substrate of undoped InAs with a Au nanoantenna at the other end. The metalens serves to focus both propagating and evanescent waves into a focal point at which the field confinement and enhancement are improved using the plasmonic nanoantenna. This paper shows the design and performance of the metalens, which has applications in subwavelength imaging and sensing.

articleTitle: Multi Band Antenna System for Energy Harvesters
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Design, and simulation of dual band planar antenna system for energy harvesting applications is given. The dual band antenna system is based on the modeling and design of microstrip octagonal patch antenna. The proposed dual band antenna has good bandwidth, gain and radiation characteristics at the frequency of interests. It has also lower profile in comparison to conventional microstrip patch antennas. The dual band antenna system is also interfaced with dual band rectifier system in the energy harvester. The performance of the antenna investigated when integrated with dc-RF rectifier and matching network. The simulation and measurement results for dual band antenna system are presented and critical antenna performance parameters when integrated with dual band energy harvesting system is discussed.

articleTitle: Active Huygens' Box: Arbitrary Synthesis of EM Waves in Metallic Cavities
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Previously, it was believed that electromagnetic plane waves cannot exist in a closed metallic cavity. However, by applying the electromagnetic equivalence principle, we have demonstrated the formation of an arbitrary waveform in a region enclosed by an active Huygens' metasurface. In this paper, we apply this principle on two cavity shapes - a rectangular and a cylindrical cavity, which we call the Huygens' boxes. We present simulation results to demonstrate the generation of traveling plane waves at 0° and 45° in both Huygens' boxes. We also present measured experimental results that agrees with the simulation results for the Huygens' box. We have thus demonstrated the generation and control of waveforms in a metallic cavity at an unprecedented level. We believe that this novel discovery will find applications in a wide range of applications like imaging, communication, and medical therapy in the nearest future.

articleTitle: Adjoint-Based Uncertainty Quantification in Frequency-Domain Double Higher-Order FEM
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We summarize an adjoint-based uncertainty quantification technique for a double higher-order finite element method solution in frequency-domain computational electromagnetics. We introduce the motivation and structure of the adjoint for the double-curl wave equation. We demonstrate scattering results for a lossy dielectric sphere.

articleTitle: Compact Tri-Band Pass Filter Using Optimized Psi-Shaped Resonators
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a compact tri-band pass filter (BPF) at 0.75 GHz, 2.1 GHz, and 3.5 GHz is introduced using a modified compact tri-mode Psi-shape resonator. The Psi-shape resonator is used to obtain three resonance frequencies and two transmission zeroes to improve the filter performance. The compact tri-band pass filter is proposed using fractal structure to reduce the size. The implemented design is simulated, fabricated, and measured. All measured results are consistent with the analysis and the simulations.

articleTitle: Loss and Starting Performance of Inverter-Fed Induction Motors Considering Semi-Closed Effect of Closed Slot
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Due to the interaction of fundamental and harmonic fields, semi-closed slot effect in iron bridge area may not only increase the leakage reactance, but also reduce the stray losses caused by harmonic flux density and high frequency current density in rotor bars, which is useful to design the inverter-fed cage induction motors. This paper analyzes the starting performance, such as slot leakage reactance, starting current and maximum torque, considering semi-closed slot effect of closed rotor bars with different parameters by FEM, meanwhile, a prototype is manufactured and the experimental validation is also carried out.

articleTitle: Energy Stable Staggered High Order Finite Differences for Optical Media
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present high order energy stable staggered summation by parts discretizations for Maxwell's equations in a non-magnetic dispersive optical medium.

articleTitle: Powerful TLM Technique for Analyzing Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a time-domain technique for analyzing antennas efficiently with the help of Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) Method is presented. This procedure requires the simulation of free space, and, the near-to- far-field transformation. Numerical, as well as experimental results are introduced and discussed, underlining the applicability of this technique for broad-band antenna design.

articleTitle: A Compact Coplanar Waveguide Quad-Band Wilkinson Power Divider Using Non-Uniform Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, varying-impedance coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission lines are used to design a fully planar quad-band Wilkinson power divider (WPD). The design equations are presented, and an optimization process is carried out to obtain the quad-band operation with a small utilization area. The proposed divider is designed to operate at 0.5, 1.3, 2.2 and 3 GHz. The divider is simulated and fabricated. Simulated and the measured results are in a very good agreement. The input port matching parameter, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, is measured to be less than -19 dB at the design frequencies. Moreover, very good output ports matching and isolation between the output ports are achieved with a transmission parameter, S21, of -3±2 dB at the design frequencies.

articleTitle: In Vitro Dielectric Properties of Rat Skin Tissue for Microwave Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Dermal tissue characterization based on dielectric properties can be utilized as a non-invasive method for diagnosis of skin cancers. To enable such technology, there is a need to develop techniques that can rapidly and accurately collect the dielectric properties of the skin tissues. Therefore, the current measurement techniques and tools has to be optimized for skin cancer detection. To this end, this study presents dielectric property measurements with open-ended coaxial probes having small apertures customized for detection of skin cancer. Relative permittivity and conductivity of rat skin tissue is characterized with open-ended coaxial probes with outer diameters of 0.9mm and 0.5mm between 0.5GHz-6GHz and the measurement results are compared with the traditional probes having diameter of 2.2mm. The results agree well with the reported literature data.

articleTitle: RF Compressed Sensing Radar Based on Digital Beamforming for Localization and IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents the concept of a radio frequency (RF) compressed sensing radar for indoor localization. A digital beamforming architecture for RF physical layer compressed sensing is discussed. Compressed sensing can reconstruct an under-sampled signal provided it is sparse in nature. A pseudo random multi-beam radiation pattern will be used to scan the target frame. The spatial sparsity in the target frame helps in recovering the entire frame using less number of scans compared to the conventional indoor localization system.

articleTitle: Fully Inkjet-Printed Tunable Flexible Microfluidic Chipless RFID Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a tunable flexible microfluidic-based sensor is proposed. The sensor is fabricated using fast, cost-effective, and environment friendly multilayer inkjet printing techniques. Three spiral resonators with microfluidic channels are designed in three different frequencies, each resonator can be tuned individually to encode 3bits information by changing the liquid in the microfluidic channels. The proposed flexible microfluidic RFID sensor can be used for applications such as liquid analysis, healthcare monitoring and wireless sensing.

articleTitle: Point Source Transmitting Power Estimation of Wireless Avionics Intra-Communication Systems Using the Large-Scale FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Wireless avionics intra-communication (WAIC) systems are operated at the same frequency bands as aircraft radio altimeters, i.e., 4,200-4,400 MHz. The coexistence conditions of WAIC systems and radio altimeters are investigated in detail with respect to electromagnetic compatibility. Firstly, the 4-GHz electromagnetic field around a three-dimensional Airbus A320 aircraft model is obtained through large-scale finite-difference time-domain analysis. Then, a transmitting antenna is modeled at the center of the aircraft at window height. Finally, the point source transmitting power at the geometrical center of the aircraft is estimated for the coexistence investigation.

articleTitle: Microwave Non-Destructive Testing Technique for Defect Detection of Composite Piles via Electromagnetic Waves with FDTD
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Radar and microwave non-destructive testing (NDT) technique is used to simulate a concrete-filled Fiber Reinforced Polymer (FRP) tubes and a concrete pile containing defects (delamination, crack, void). The delamination that occurs as a result of external factors is modeled as closest to the reality. Interaction of electromagnetic wave and the concrete pile is utilized for numerical simulation. A Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method with Perfectly Matched Layer (PML) Absorbing Boundary Condition (ABC) is proposed to simulate electromagnetic wave propagation in FRP tube and composite pile. 2D simulation of a wave generated from a point source at microwave frequencies is obtained by using MATLAB®.

articleTitle: Impedance Matching of Layered Structures with Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Impedance matching of layered structures involving metamaterial is investigated. The base isotropic material is selected from commonly used microwave materials with dielectric permittivity ranging from 2.1 to 10.2, such as Teflon and Alumina. The method adapted is immune to polarization of the incident wave regardless if it is TE or TM wave. The metamaterial permittivity and permeability parameters are obtained for the minimum reflectivity by varying the thickness of the metamaterial for each isotropic material for broad range of incident angles and operational frequency. The results presented in this paper can be used for applications where antireflection (AR) is a requirement.

articleTitle: Impedance-Matched High-Index Ceramic Microwave Metamaterials at X-Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we present a design to achieve both impedance matching and high refractive index using dielectric metamaterial resonators in the X-band. This design is based on two cubic dielectric resonators using commercially-available high- K ceramic. By scaling the size and lattice constant of the individual units, the first magnetic resonance of one cube and the first electric resonance of the other cube can be overlapped in order to achieve the design criteria. The proposed design is then compared with the dielectric Huygens' surfaces inspired by the work of Kivshar, et. al. [1], which is based on a single cylindrical dielectric resonator. For our case, we find that the two-cube resonator design has better performance than the single cylindrical resonator. Thus, it can achieve the reflection-less surface, referred to as a Huygens' surface, and create a high index of refraction at the same time.

articleTitle: Modeling and Experiments of High-Quality Factor Cavity Shielding Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the coupling from external electromagnetic (EM) fields to the interior EM fields of a high-quality factor cylindrical cavity through a small perturbing slot. We illustrate the shielding effectiveness versus frequency, highlighting bounds on the penetrant power through the slot. Because internal fields may become larger than external ones, we then introduce a small amount of microwave absorbing materials decorating the slot to improve shielding effectiveness considerably, as shown by both simulations and experiments. Although the cylindrical cavity is used for demonstration purposes in this paper, the conclusions presented here can be leveraged for use with more complex cavity structures.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation and Analyses of SAR Images from Ship Wakes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The study of SAR images from ship wakes is of great value to the detection and information inversion of ship targets in a marine environment. In this paper, a facet-based simplified small-slope approximation (FBS-SSA) is used to investigate the electromagnetic (EM) scattering from a sea surface with Kelvin wakes, based on which the SAR echoes can be simulated. Then, SAR images are readily obtained with the range-Doppler algorithm (RDA). SAR images under different incident angles, ship directions are analyzed, it is concluded that for a low incident angle, wakes show more clearly due to an obvious comparison of strong scatters and weak scatters. In addition, both the transverse and divergent waves can be seen when SAR flies across ship heading while only divergent waves can be seen when SAR flies along ship heading. Only one arm can be seen when the angle between SAR's flight direction and ship's heading is 45°.

articleTitle: Design Trade-Offs for Spline-Parameterized Patch Coupler Through Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Investigations of design trade-offs for a miniaturized patch coupler are presented. Using surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization, a set of designs representing available compromises between the coupler bandwidth and footprint area are obtained and analyzed. Sequential domain patching is utilized as the optimization engine to maintain acceptable computational cost despite a large number of design parameters. The presented approach is illustrated using a spline-parameterized coupler operating at 5.6 GHz.

articleTitle: On Higher-Order Nyström Discretization of Scalar Potential Integral Equation for Penetrable Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: finite difference time-domain analysis; Maxwell equations; finite element analysis; antenna radiation patterns; optimisation; time-domain analysis; electromagnetic wave scattering; plasmonics; computational electromagnetics; optical metamaterials.

articleTitle: An Integrated, Broadband Circularly-Polarized Millimeter-Wave Metasurface-Based Transmit-Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of an integrated circularly-polarized high-gain antenna with a broad bandwidth at the millimeter-wave Ka-band. The proposed compact antenna is enabled by the integration of a metasurfaces-based transmit-array and a broadband circularly-polarized feed radiator. The feed radiator is a substrate integrated waveguide fed patch with a finite-sized metasurfaces superstrate, while the transmit-array utilizes the rotation phase for collimating the waves emitted from the feeding source. The full-wave simulation results show that the integrated transmit-array antenna achieves an overall bandwidth of about 18.3% within which the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> is below -10 dB, the axial ratio is smaller than 3 dB, and the gain variation is less than 3 dB with a peak gain of 23.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Food Contamination via Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Detecting food contamination in products moving along the production chain is a priority for every established food producer. Although detection technologies have been widely used in last years, low-density foreign bodies such as plastic, thin glass or wood are still undetectable to all established detection systems. Hence, the use of microwave imaging system to be used along the production chain is proposed in this work. This scenario implies a reduced time for data gathering and hence a limited amount of available data. To face this issue, an imaging system taking advantage of the targets movement and of the expected small size of the sought contamination is developed. The rationale of the approach is described and assessed in a simple, yet meaningful case.

articleTitle: Induction Heating of Thermoplastic Composites in the Presence of a Susceptor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The issue of inductive heating and welding of two pieces of thermoplastic composites in the presence of a susceptor alloy consisting of 67% nickel and 27% copper is studied using Maxwell. Simulation results clearly show solid losses in the material which can be used to heat and weld the composite panels. Location based temperature increase due to I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>R losses are calculated which show significant heating and welding potentials.

articleTitle: FEKO™ Analysis of Surface Treatments for Mitigating the EM Coupling Between Conformal Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Conformal antenna arrays that are embedded in the same planar or convex curved surface can interfere with each other via the electromagnetic waves propagating along the surface. Various surface treatments on a metallic ground plane for suppressing the surface waves are investigated using FEKO™ with numerical and layered media Green's functions solutions. These include metallic fences, corrugations, radar absorbing structures (RAS), and thin magnetic radar absorbing materials (magRAM). It is found that magRAM offers the best trade-off between wideband surface wave suppression and low profile.

articleTitle: 3D Diagonalization and Supplementation of Maxwell's Magneto-Static Field Equations in Fully Anisotropic and Inhomogeneous Media - Part I: Proof of Existence by Construction
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Consider the Maxwell's magneto-static equations ∇×H=J and ∇·B=0 in fully anisotropic and inhomogeneous media characterized by the 3 × 3 positive-definite permeability matrix μ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3×3</sup>(x, y, z). This paper establishes - for the first time - that the aforementioned system of the governing and constitutive equations can be diagonalized with respect to the arbitrarily chosen z-axis leading to the Dc - and the associated supplementary Sc -forms. The existence of the (Dc,Sc) -forms is demonstrated by construction. The accompanying paper (Part II) proves the internal consistency of the (Dc,Sc) -forms rigorously by showing the sharp equivalence of the (Dc, Sc) -forms with the originating Maxwell's and constitutive equations.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Three-Dimensional Nanoantennas for Metasurface Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recent advances in manufacturing techniques have been made to match the demand for high performance optical devices. To this end, tremendous research activity has been focused on optical metasurfaces as they offer a unique potential to achieve disruptive designs when paired with innovative fabrication techniques and inverse design tools. However, most metasurface designs have revolved around canonical geometries. While these elements are relatively easy to fabricate, they represent only a small portion of the design space, and rarely offer peak performance in transmission, phase range or field of view. In this work, a Lazy Ant Colony Optimization (LACO) technique is applied in conjunction with a full-wave solver using the Periodic Finite Element Boundary Integral (PFEBI) method to reveal high performing three-dimensional nanoantenna designs with potential applications for a variety of optical devices.

articleTitle: Validation of Wind Turbine Doppler Signatures in a Passive Bistatic Radar with a Point Scatterer Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a study on Doppler signatures of wind turbines in a passive bistatic radar system (PBR). Measurements of the turbine blades from a PBR operating in the UHF region are compared with a theoretical model derived from the assumption of point scatterers.

articleTitle: Platform-Aware In-Situ Antenna and Metamaterial Analysis and Design
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to build a reconfigurable, reusable, and parallel model reduction platform towards transformative in-situ antenna design. The key idea is to introduce a separable and compressible platform Green's function in an up-front offline computation. Once obtained, the online computational complexity does not depend on the size of the in-situ platform. As a result, in-situ design and optimization of multi-antenna systems can be performed at the same cost as the free-space radiation. The advancements make high-fidelity in-situ antenna design orders of magnitude faster.

articleTitle: High-Performance Metasurfaces Synthesized via Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Metasurfaces show extreme promise for realizing disruptive optical devices due to their ability to tailor reflection and transmission properties at a surface by exploiting the generalized form of Snell's law. Moreover, polarization-, angular-and frequency-dependent performances can also be engineered to achieve dispersive behaviors desired for a particular application. However, how one designs a metasurface that achieves high performances in several of these areas simultaneously is generally not clear. Therefore, synthesizing high-performance metasurfaces requires employing powerful optimization techniques in the inverse design process. To this end, state-of-the-art multi-objective optimization algorithms offer the potential to realize metasurfaces that meet multiple design goals while also presenting the tradeoffs between competing objectives.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Dual-Band, Electrically Small, Printed Octafilar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents several innovative techniques for the design and optimization of a dual band octafilar helix antenna. The antenna was designed to fit inside a radome with. 07λ diameter. This was achieved through a novel technique of applying differing pitches and terminations to the upper and lower frequency antenna filars and then feeding them from the same point at the base. The final design produced gain greater than 0dBic at zenith across both. 07*F1 bands of operation. The differing pitch approach to the elements was seen to improve impedance and hence overall gain performance at the low frequency band by about 2 dBic.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Electrical Properties Tomography Using a Simplified Contrast-Source Inversion Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The contrast source inversion (CSI) method is a well-known inversion technique that has been utilized in a wide range of application areas. Here we show that in the specific situation of electrical properties tomography (EPT) in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which is a so-called hybrid inverse problem, since data is collected inside the reconstruction domain, the CSI method can be simplified to what is essentially a single forward simulation provided the electromagnetic field has an E-polarized field structure. As a consequence, the computational costs are significantly reduced and our experiments show that reconstructions obtained with the simplified CSI method have essentially the same accuracy as reconstructions obtained with the full CSI inversion method.

articleTitle: Discontinuous Galerkin Time Domain Method for Periodic Dispersive Structure Analysis at Oblique Incidence
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An efficient discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method is presented to analyze the electromagnetic scattering from periodic structures with dispersive components. The time domain periodic boundary conditions are implemented in the DGTD method by introducing transformed field variables. The method is applied to the Drude dispersive media model using an auxiliary differential equation (ADE) approach. Numerical analysis of a dual-band infrared absorber is shown to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Effective Electromagnetic Parameter Extractions for Porous Media Using a Potential-Based Formulation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a potential-based partial differential formulation is utilized to extract the effective electromagnetic parameters of multiphase porous media. To overcome the low-frequency catastrophe, the magnetic vector and electric scalar potentials are employed to formulate the vector wave equation that governs the electromagnetic problems. The magnetic vector potential is then gauged by the generalized Lorentz gauge, which is supplemented to the vector wave equation to form a complete system of equations. It is shown that, after a proper discretization of the resulting potential-based formulation, the low-frequency breakdown issue is successfully removed without the need to perform a tree-cotree splitting and the effective parameters of the porous media can be extracted in a wide frequency range with an excellent accuracy.

articleTitle: The Optimization of Arbitrary-Shape Conformal Array Antenna's Performance Based on CSHPSO
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to optimize the arbitrary-shape conformal array antenna's performance, the Cloud Self-adaptive Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization (CSHPSO) is introduced in this paper. The inertia weight coefficient is introduced into Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization (HPSO), which is built upon PSO, to avoid the premature convergence. The introduction of cloud self-adaptive model makes particles in HPSO more intelligent. An arbitrary-shape conformal array is optimized by CSHPSO and results show that the gain is improved compared with the situation that all elements are excited. It is obvious that the algorithm is effective to optimize arbitrary-shape conformal array antenna's performance such as gain, beam-width and side-lobe.

articleTitle: FDTD Simulation of Multilayer-Coated and Rough Surface Metals Using Surface Impedance Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A surface impedance method with synchronization in time and its application to the FDTD simulation of multilayer-coated metals and rough surface metals are presented. The numerical results showed that the presented method is accurate and efficient.

articleTitle: Generation and Manipulation of OAM Beams in 2D Planar Arrays and Reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we develop methods of manipulating OAM beams by using distribution of excitation coefficients in a 2D aperture. The excitation coefficients applied are useful for 2D arrays, reflectarray and reflector antennas. Specifically, we study the effect of spiral phase across the aperture, radial phase gradient in the aperture and gaussian amplitude distribution in the aperture. It is noted that spiral phasing controls the OAM index, radial-phasing controls the beam position and Gaussian amplitude distribution reduces the ripples in the beam-ridge along azimuthal direction.

articleTitle: A Boundary Element Method (BEM) for Modeling the Nonlocal Hydrodynamic Response in Deep-Nm Plasmonic Wire Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, we present a Boundary Element Method (BEM) for modeling the optical response from a deep nanometric metallic wire waveguide with an arbitrary transverse cross section. Instead of using a local parameter, i.e. permittivity, to describe the electromagnetic (EM) property of the material constituting the guide, a nonlocal hydrodynamic model is considered to give a much finer description for the detailed dynamics of conduction electrons in the metal. Together with this nonlocal model, Maxwell's equations are solved within the framework of the Boundary Element Method (BEM). The numerical result is contrasted with the analytical one and a very good agreement is seen.

articleTitle: Radiated EM Flux Based Diagnostic Approach for Stator Insulation Failures in Inverter Fed Motors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Analysis of harmonics and inter-harmonics components in the spectrum of the radiated electromagnetic (EM) field is proposed for the detection of induction motor (IM) windings' insulation failure. The IM is fed through a voltage source inverter (VSI) operating under the classical direct torque controller (DTC). To investigate the EM spectrum, the radiated magnetic field intensity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vec{H})$</tex> was calculated at an observer point in a physics-based finite element analysis (FEA) platform.

articleTitle: Platform-Aware In-Situ Antenna and Metamaterial Analysis and Design
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to build a reconfigurable, reusable, and parallel model reduction platform towards transformative in-situ antenna design. The key idea is to introduce a separable and compressible platform Green's function in an up-front offline computation. Once obtained, the online computational complexity does not depend on the size of the in-situ platform. As a result, in-situ design and optimization of multi-antenna systems can be performed at the same cost as the free-space radiation. The advancements make high-fidelity in-situ antenna design orders of magnitude faster.

articleTitle: Tensor Decompositions for Reducing the Memory Requirement of Translation Operator Tensors in FMM-FFT Accelerated IE Solvers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Tensor decompositions are applied to lessen the memory requirements of translation operator tensors in fast multipole method-fast Fourier transform (FMM-FFT) accelerated integral equation (IE) solvers. In particular, methodologies leveraging Tucker and tensor train (TT) decompositions are developed to compress the three-dimensional (3D) arrays and four-dimensional (4D) array storing the FFT'ed translation operator values. Preliminary results show the achieved memory reduction as well as imposed computational overhead via the developed methodologies.

articleTitle: A Novel Mid-Infrared Metalens Using a Hyperbolic Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel metalens in the mid infrared range from 6.4um to 10um is designed. It consists of a plasmonic waveguide coupler (PWC), on a slab of type I hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) on the top of a substrate of undoped InAs with a Au nanoantenna at the other end. The metalens serves to focus both propagating and evanescent waves into a focal point at which the field confinement and enhancement are improved using the plasmonic nanoantenna. This paper shows the design and performance of the metalens, which has applications in subwavelength imaging and sensing.

articleTitle: A Numerical Approach of Graphene Non-Linear Electromagnetic Response
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In the present work, graphene non-linear phenomena are introduced in the finite-difference time-domain algorithm through the dynamic evaluation of its surface conductivity at each time-step. The latter is influenced via the action of the carrier density on graphene that is significantly altered when strong excitation is applied. The developed algorithm is validated by the quantification of the normal propagation distortion.

articleTitle: Efficient RCS Evaluation for the Conventional TF/SF Separation Model in the FDTD Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A systematic radar cross-section (RCS) evaluation scheme to enhance the total-field/scattered-field (TF/SF) separation scheme is developed in this paper for the nonstandard finite-difference time-domain (NS-FDTD) and FDTD method. Usually, the direct launch of an electromagnetic wave on the TF/SF separation surface generates undesired scattered artifacts. To avoid the influence of these forms in RCS, we introduce an error prediction model via pre-calculated data from vector parasites. It is numerically shown that our technique can improve the reliability of the RCS analysis for aircrafts with electrically large size.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based FDTD Accelerators for 2DEG Plasma-Wave Device Modeling at THz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Plasmonic waves supported on 2DEG devices at terahertz (THz) frequencies are important for future high-bandwidth wireless communication and imaging systems. The design of such devices requires solution of computationally intensive Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) based multiphysics models which can be slow even with the use of GPUs. In this work, application-specific custom computing architectures based on reconfigurable deep nano-CMOS FPGA technologies, such as the 14nm Xilinx ZynQ RF SoC, are explored for solving the above problem using massively-parallel fine-grain pipelined multirate systolic-array processors.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Slot Dipole with AMC Using Textiles
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A dual band slot dipole antenna integrated with an AMC plane is proposed to reduce SAR when operated on body for WBAN applications. The AMC plane is formed using a 3 × 3 array of unit cells, each consisting of a square patch integrated with diamond-shaped slot. Results indicate that the antenna provides wide upper bandwidth up to 600 MHz (in flat condition) and up to 570 MHz when bent. Besides that, its front-to-back ratio (FBR) is also improved.

articleTitle: An Origami Based Capacity Resilient and Reconfigurable MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, the ability of a physically reconfigurable, linear uniform, MIMO antenna with variable interelement spacing to achieve maximum capacity is demonstrated for a variety of propagation scenarios. Propagation scenarios are differentiated based upon the angle of incidence. An example situation with two transmit and two receive antennas is analyzed. It is shown that the maximum capacity is achieved by appropriately selecting the inter-element spacing for different propagation scenarios. Demonstrating the resilience of this reconfigurable antenna, high throughput communications are allowed to be reliably achieved.

articleTitle: Axial PML Performance Near the Axis of Rotation in Cylindrical FDTD
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This work investigates the effect of proximity to the axis of rotation on the perfectly-matched-layer (PML) absorbing boundary condition when used to truncate cylindrical finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations along the axial dimension. The investigation is based on deriving predictive equations for the overall reflection coefficient off the innermost PML interface which rely heavily on a recently derived numerical dispersion relation for cylindrical FDTD. Accounting for cylindrical waves behavior near the axis of rotation is critical in realizing appropriate cylindrical FDTD and PML performance near the axis of rotation.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Plasmonic Metasurface Absorber for Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A plasmonic dual-band polarization-insensitive metasurface absorber is proposed. The design provides subwavelength and confined collection of the absorbed energy in the gaps of the structure. In this paper, we study the absorption behavior of the metasurface operating in a dual-band mode targeting the mid-infrared range suitable for energy harvesting applications such as thermophotovoltaics. The design is optimized using a global optimization technique.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Multilayer Rectangular Coils for Wireless Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, miniaturized multilayer rectangular printed circuit board (PCB) coils are investigated and, a method for calculating the total self-inductance, mutual inductance, and power transfer efficiency between two miniature (6.6mm × 6.6mm) coils for wireless power transfer applications is presented. First, in order to reduce the complexity, coil trace turns are modeled as rectangular loops. A formula based on integral solution starting from Biot - Savart's law gives the analytical results of the mutual inductances between each rectangular trace in same and different layers. Then 4-layer rectangular PCB coil based wireless power transfer system is modeled, analyzed and simulated. Mutual inductance and power transfer efficiency parameters according to the distance between coils and trace width of the coils are calculated with analytical methods. Achieved inductance and power transfer efficiency results from the analytical model and simulation results in Ansys - Maxwell and Simplorer environment is compared for verification. The analytical approach proposed in this paper is provide a fast mutual inductance and power transfer efficiency calculation for multilayer rectangular printed circuit board inductors compared to the simulation.

articleTitle: A Simple Test for Quickly Measuring Shielding Effectiveness of Connectors Using Isotropic Broadband Electric Field Probe
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The shielding of coaxial cables and connectors is an important parameter for the electromagnetic compatibility of electro-electronic systems. It is of paramount importance the detection of failures as soon as possible in order to consider improved systems and avoid unexpected costs. Within this context, this paper presents a simple procedure to measure the electric field radiated by connectors, with and without solder. A virtual simulation was performed using the commercial package FEKO with a good correlation between simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Effect of Cell Curvature on the Convergence Rates of EFIE Numerical Solutions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The convergence rate of higher-order numerical solutions in electromagnetics depends on the fidelity of the target model, specifically on the order of curvature used in that model when analyzing curved targets. The effect of patch curvature is explored for canonical targets such as spheres and disks where exact reference solutions are available for comparison.

articleTitle: A Simple Methodology to Eliminate Noise in the Antennas Dipoles Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The Measurements of dipole antenna outside the shielded room or semi anechoic chamber using an oscilloscope most often present problems due to the high input impedance of the dipole at low frequencies. The oscilloscope is susceptible to noise in low frequencies and 50 and 60 Hz is often the greatest signal received. Within this context, this paper presents a simple procedure with low costs to solve this problem.

articleTitle: Determining the Dispersive Features of Nanophotonic Structures Based on Hybrid FEM/TMM Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Determining the dispersion relation of nanophotonic structures is one of the biggest challenges especially for nano-scale inhomogeneous structures where several efforts have been directed. Here, we present a technique that leverages the accuracy and simplicity of the combination of transfer matrix method (TMM) and finite element method (FEM). This hybrid technique allows us to find the spatial dispersion, coupling strength and nature of the generated modes.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Resonances and Light Generation in Nanoparticle Dimers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We numerically study nanoparticle dimer (two closely-spaced nanoparticles) with the aim to resolve gap plasmon mode using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. Our semi-conformal meshing based on transformation optics principles allows for accurate accounting of nanoparticle gaps and other curved shapes. We calculate surface plasmon amplification by stimulated emission of radiation (SPASER) in the dimer modes using Bloch equations.

Author Keywords: surface plasmon amplification by stimulated emission of radiation

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Dual-Band and Double-Polarization IR Perfect Absorbers Using Adjoint Sensitivities
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, we utilize adjoint sensitivity approach within a constrained optimization algorithm to design a dual band infrared perfect absorber (IR-PA). The structure is composed of a silver circular ring and an elliptic cross centered on top of a two layer substrate. Dimensions of the ring and crossed ellipses in addition to the thicknesses are considered the design parameters. Careful parameters' optimization leads to a dual-band and near unity absorber at 2.7 μm and 6.0 μm, respectively. The symmetry of the design allows the operation at a polarization free electromagnetic excitation. The absorption peak wavelengths and their bandwidths can be tailored to match with a wide range of applications such as detection, energy harvesting, imaging, and stealth technologies.

articleTitle: Driveability Optimization of HEV Powertrain
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The work investigates the optimization of a Hybrid Electric Vehicle, HEV, powertrain to achieve good driveability (comfort). This involves the development of a robust identifier utilizing state space, SS, models and electromagnetic, EM, field computations to predict accurately the performance of the powertrain and a Fuzzy Logic, FL, based algorithm to ensure good driveability. The developed model is applied in a case study of a HEV and the predicted simulation results are validated by comparison to readily available benchmark data.

articleTitle: Lightning Performance of Overhead Distribution Lines with Underbuilt Ground Wires
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
