abstract: We investigate the improvement of the lightning performance of overhead distribution lines by additional ground wires placed beneath phase conductors. We adopt a time-domain method based on the matrix formalism of multiconductor (MTL) transmission lines that allows for the computation of overvoltages across insulator strings, when direct lightning hits a tower or a ground wire.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Branch-Line Coupler with Enhanced Bandwidth for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Dual-band operation with enhanced bandwidth and small size are important performance figures of hybrid couplers for applications in modern communication systems. Unfortunately, maintaining broad frequency ranges of operation stays in conflict with circuit miniaturization. In this work, a compact dual-band branch-line coupler (BLC) with improved bandwidth has been proposed. Electrical performance of the structure has been improved by introducing an asymmetry into the cross-coupled branches of the reference dual-band circuit. The coupler has been optimized at a low computational cost using a surrogate-assisted method. It features 180 MHz and 450 MHz bandwidths at the center frequencies of 2.45 GHz and 5.4 GHz, respectively. The footprint of the optimized circuit is only 296 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The coupler has been benchmarked against competitive dual-band BLCs from the literature.

articleTitle: FDTD Modeling of Lightning Electromagnetic Field Propagation Over Mountainous Terrain
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The Full-Wave Finite-Difference-Time-Domain (FDTD) electromagnetic (EM) simulation method can simulate large domains and produce time-marching solutions for arbitrary time-domain sources, making it ideal for many lightning applications. In this paper, a two-dimensional (2D) axial-symmetric and a three-dimensional (3D) FDTD model are developed that include irregular terrain based on real topographic data. The models open the door to a wide variety of advanced modeling applications in the analysis of the lightning EM field propagation over mountainous terrain and the location error of lightning location systems (LLSs) in the presence of in mountainous regions.

articleTitle: Geometrically Conformal Quadrilateral Surface-Reconstruction for MoM-SIE Simulations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a higher order quadrilateral surface remeshing approach for application to the method of moments. We briefly introduce the motivation for high-quality quadrilateral meshes for accurate and efficient application of cutting edge integration and singularity extraction approaches. Results are demonstrated for simple surfaces and compared with a common quadrilateral remeshing algorithm.

articleTitle: Modeling of All-Dielectric Metasurfaces Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach using deep neural networks to model all-dielectric meta-atoms over a wide spectrum. A deep neural network is constructed and fully trained in a supervised way to predict the performance of dielectric meta-atoms. The proposed approach has been validated by comparing the obtained results with full-wave simulation results.

articleTitle: A Method-of-Lines Time Domain Method Solver for Dispersive Bianisotropic Maxwell's Equations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Motivated by the emergence of dispersive, bianisotropic materials occurring as an effective medium model of metamaterials, we develop a time-domain algorithm capable of simulating general dispersive, bianisotropic media. This method utilizes auxiliary differential equations for the polarization and magnetization, which are solved in conjunction with Maxwell's equations using a method-of-lines approach with high-order finite-differences in space and integrated using the fourth order Runga-Kutta method.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Networks Based Surrogate Model for Topology Optimization of Electromagnetic Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work a novel approach is presented for topology optimization of low frequency electromagnetic devices. In particular a surrogate model based on deep neural networks with encoder-decoder architecture is introduced. A first autoencoder deep neural network learns to represent the input images that describe the topology, i.e. geometry and materials. The novel idea is to use the low dimensional output space of the encoder as the search space of the optimization algorithm, instead of using the higher dimensional space represented by the input images. A second deep neural network learns the relationship between the encoder outputs and the objective function (i.e., torque), which is calculated by means of a finite element analysis. The calculation time for the optimization is greatly improved by reducing the dimensionality of the search space, and by introducing the surrogate model, whereas the quality of the result is slightly affected.

articleTitle: 2D Integral Formulation with High Order Impedance Boundary Conditions for Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: High order impedance boundary conditions take into account the curvature of the conductive surface and the diffusion of the electromagnetic field in all directions into the conductor. A previously published two dimensional boundary integral formulation based on magnetic vector potential and perturbation theory is compared here with the corresponding non-perturbative version. Some of the limitations of the perturbative approach are shown and overcome by the present formulation.

articleTitle: Radio Astronomy Techniques for Multistatic Radar Imaging and Localization of Space Objects
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper explores the application of aperture synthesis techniques for radio astronomy to multistatic radar with the goal of improving image quality and relative positioning precision for practical array geometries. In a step towards achieving this goal, a new multistatic radar approach is proposed that incorporates aperture synthesis processing. The feasibility of this approach is demonstrated via analytical results and simulation. The approach is then compared to conventional multistatic radar processing, where, for the same geometry, the conventional method is found to produce superior reconstructions in terms of signal-to-sidelobe level. However, the proposed approach is advantageous for two reasons. First, if a radio astronomy array and correlator already exist, the new method will generate acceptable images. Second, timing and synchronization requirements on the transmitters can be relaxed in the new method, allowing low-cost, low-complexity transmitters to be utilized.

articleTitle: A New Perspective on an Old Problem: Scattering by a Perfect Electric Conductor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We explore several different singular surface integral equation formulations. These formulations are specifically designed for time-harmonic scattering by a perfect electric conductor and are obtained by choosing non-conventional boundary unknowns.

articleTitle: CW Radar Operation in the Focused Near-Field
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper we will show by computer simulation and by measurements that the horn antennas of a bi-static radar operating in the near-field have a distinct maximum at a non-zero range. By focusing the antennas on this hot spot a low-powered, continuous-wave Ku-band radar could detect flying mosquitoes at very short range.

articleTitle: Advanced Computational Methods for Transparency Control of Low Emissivity Windows
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Low emissivity (low-E) windows have thin layers of metallic oxides for extra thermal insulation. These metallic layers not only block infrared and ultraviolet waves but also attenuate cellular signals. Cellular coverage can be improved by using Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) layers that will act as bandpass filters, instead of solid layers. This paper discusses the type of FSS structures that can be integrated into the window glass. A workflow process is demonstrated for efficient design and analysis of such structures using Periodic Boundary Conditions (PBC), Characterised Surfaces in conjunction with Ray-Launching Geometrical Optics (RL-GO) method.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Different Formulations for an Inverse Source Magnetostatic Problem
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The resolution of inverse problems is a quite common task in the diagnostic processes based on electromagnetic field measurements, in particular when internal characteristics of the object under test are to be estimated from external measurements. This class of problems are well known to be ill posed, and a number of different techniques have been proposed to make the estimation process reliable. In this paper, with reference to an application in the framework of low frequency magnetic fields measurements, the effects of different choices for the degrees of freedom are discussed, with the aim of improving the solution reliability.

articleTitle: 3D Diagonalization and Supplementation of Maxwell's Magneto-Static Field Equations in Fully Anisotropic and Inhomogeneous Media - Part II: Relative Proof of Consistency
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Consider the Maxwell's magneto-static equations ∇×H=J and ∇·B=0 in fully anisotropic and inhomogeneous media characterized by the 3 × 3 positive-definite position-dependent permeability matrix μ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3×3</sup>(x, y, z). In the accompanying paper (Part I) the existence of the diagonalized Dc - and the associated supplementary Sc -forms was demonstrated constructively. In this paper the internal consistency of the (Dc, Sc) - forms is established rigorously by proving the sharp equivalence of the (Dc, Sc) -forms with the originating Maxwell's and constitutive equations.

articleTitle: Recent Improvements in Feko
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper describes the latest improvements to the commercial electromagnetic software Feko. These include the hybridization of the MLFMM based on the surface equivalence principle, the finite element method and windscreen antenna analysis; periodic boundary conditions are accelerated and extended to support the finite element method; and the number of options to model a cable shield has been extended to include direct modeling of a double shield and single-layered braided shield formulas described by Tyni and Demoulin.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Emitter for Thermophotovoltaics: Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A metasurface-based thermophotovoitaics system directly converts thermal radiation to electricity through the photovoitaic effect. The efficiency of such a system significantly depends on the thermal stability and efficiency of the spectral reshaping of the metasurface. We couple the generative adversarial network technique with the topology optimization to design a new class of high-efficiency metasurface thermal emitters. Numerical simulations confirm that due to non-trivial metasurface topologies the proposed method generates the close-to-ultimate high-efficiency emitters. Comparison with a conventional global optimization technique shows that our topology-optimized designs demonstrate superior spectral control of thermal blackbody radiation than the regular-shape emitters optimized with conventional optimization.

articleTitle: Computation of Fields from a Magnetic Dipole in a Conductive Medium Using the QS-DGTD Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Loop antennas are often used for field generation in low-frequency electromagnetic applications. Since the antenna dimensions are much smaller than the wavelength, the antenna can accurately be replaced by its equivalent magnetic dipole model in simulations. In this paper, low-frequency magnetic dipole radiation fields in a conductive medium are computed using a three-dimensional discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain (DGTD) scheme. It is shown that this computation can be accelerated using a material scaling scheme under Quasi-Static (QS) approximation, i.e., time step size can be scaled up without sacrificing from the accuracy and the stability of the time marching scheme. Radiated fields from a magnetic dipole in a conductive medium computed by this accelerated scheme are compared to those obtained using analytical expressions. Results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: FEM-MTLN Hybridization Technique to Evaluate Electrical Current on Multiconductor Cables Inside Enclosures Illuminated by a Plane Wave
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a strategy to evaluate current on multiconductor electrical cables installed inside enclosures. This strategy consists of the hybridization of a FEM and a MTLN approach. The motivation of this strategy relies on the fact that the high order FEM scheme has less numerical dispersive effect than a usual first order scheme such as an FDTD scheme. More accuracy is thereby obtained in the MTLN response. This property is demonstrated on a generic test case configuration.

articleTitle: Measurement and Modeling of Magnetostriction in Transformer Core Based on a BPNN Method Assisted with Levenberg-Marquardt Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The reasons causing the vabriations and noises of transformer cores include the magnetostrictive force in the core material and electromagnetic forces acting on lapped seams of cores and among silicon steel sheets. This paper carried out the measurement of magnetostrictive strains in a grain-oriented steel sheet under alternating magnetizations and dicussed the effect of a dc bias present in the exciting current on the magnetostriction. Based on the experimental data, the magnetostrictive characteristics are modeled by a back propagation neural network (BPNN) method. In order to achive an acceptable convergence condition, the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm instead of the traditional gradient descent algorithm was employed to assist the BPNN.

articleTitle: Multicsale Multiphysics Modeling of Terahertz Emissions from Field Effect Transistors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, we show that indeed terahertz emissions are possible from a field effect transistors (FETs) under an influence of strong DC bias under cryogenic conditions and asymmetrical boundary conditions. Such emissions have been hypothesized by researchers in the community, by using analytical models and have been subject of much controversy in terahertz electronics field. Here by using finite-difference-time domain (FDTD) and hydrodynamic modeling, we show that such emissions are indeed possible in the high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs). Specifically, multiphysics modeling tools are developed, and simulations are conducted to demonstrate the terahertz emission phenomenology and effect of device parameters.

articleTitle: Hermite Methods for Electromagnetic Waves in Dispersive Media
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We describe arbitrary-order discretization methods based on Hermite-Birkhoff interpolation for Maxwell's equations in dispersive media. We consider generalized Lorentz models, not only for the permittivity, but also for the permeability to account for approximations to negative index metamaterials. Both conservative and dissipative methods are considered.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis of Multilayer Structures with Arbitrarily Shaped Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A general formulation for electromagnetic analysis of multilayer structures with arbitrarily shaped interfaces is presented. The formulation belongs to modal methods. Its originality lies in the use of coordinates systems attached to the profile shape of the interfaces that separate the layers and to Maxwell's equations written under the covariant form. Each interface coincides with a coordinate surface which makes it elementary to enforce boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Coupled Structural-Electromagnetic Analysis of Origami-Inspired Adaptive Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This article proposes a method to conduct coupled structural-electromagntic analysis of embedded electromagnetic devices on origami-inspired structures that are deployable and reconfigurable. The method uses a script-based multidisciplinary design and computational anaylsis tool to connect an in-house MATLAB code for nonlinear mechanics analysis and a Python-HFSS library for electromagnetic analysis.

articleTitle: The Impact of Surface Roughness on Avalanche Frequency
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: IMPATT diodes were designed and fabricated in standard CMOS technology to study the impact of the RMS value of surface roughness on the avalanche frequency. By comparing the on-chip measurements of an IMPATT diode integrated in a CPW to an integrated one with a microstrip patch antenna at the same biasing conditions, the results demonstrated a reduction in the avalanche frequency in the antenna integrated structure by 34% compared to the CPW one. Such variation is strongly associated with the increase in the conduction losses by 40%~80% based on the biasing conditions and hence the avalanche frequency.

articleTitle: Geometrically Conformal Quadrilateral Surface-Reconstruction for MoM-SIE Simulations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a higher order quadrilateral surface remeshing approach for application to the method of moments. We briefly introduce the motivation for high-quality quadrilateral meshes for accurate and efficient application of cutting edge integration and singularity extraction approaches. Results are demonstrated for simple surfaces and compared with a common quadrilateral remeshing algorithm.

articleTitle: An Accurate Technique for Modeling Realistic Well-Logging Sensors Inside Complex Media
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a pseudoanalytical mode-matching formulation is introduced for the analysis of electromagnetic well-logging tools. We present numerical results for several representative scenarios to validate and explore the input (self) impedance of typical logging-while-drilling (LWD) sensors comprised by an array of coil antennas. Preliminary conclusions are presented and the potential of this approach for modeling realistic LWD sensors is then summarized.

articleTitle: Phonon-Polariton Resonances in Hexagonal Boron Nitride Transdimensional Lattices
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We analyze optical antennas made of hexagonal boron nitride which is a natural material with hyperbolic dispersion in mid-infrared range. The antennas in the periodic array support phonon-polariton resonances including electric and magnetic dipoles and higher multipoles. The resonances are controlled by the size and shape of the antenna as well as period of the array. We regard these arrays as transdimensional lattices because of their 2D/3D translational nature. The antenna resonances allow for efficient control of light scattering, reflection, and propagation and can be utilized in metasurfaces and flat optical components.

articleTitle: An Accurate Technique for Modeling Realistic Well-Logging Sensors Inside Complex Media
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a pseudoanalytical mode-matching formulation is introduced for the analysis of electromagnetic well-logging tools. We present numerical results for several representative scenarios to validate and explore the input (self) impedance of typical logging-while-drilling (LWD) sensors comprised by an array of coil antennas. Preliminary conclusions are presented and the potential of this approach for modeling realistic LWD sensors is then summarized.

articleTitle: Co-Channel Simultaneous Transmit and Receive with 3-Element Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A novel co-polarized wideband array antenna is proposed for co-channel simultaneous transmit and receive (C-STAR) applications. The proposed C-STAR configuration is composed of three (spiral) antennas sequentially rotated by 120° Two antennas are used for transmitting (TX) and one for receiving (RX) or vice versa. The high isolation is achieved in this approach by utilizing antennas' orientation, symmetry, and phase cancellation to ideally eliminate the coupled TX signals at the RX port. To demonstrate the performance of the proposed C-STAR configuration, numerical modelling is conducted using method of moments (MoM) solver.

articleTitle: A Modified Polynomial Chaos Modeling Approach for Uncertainty Quantification
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Uncertainty quantification is a key element for modeling high speed circuits, which is often done with Monte Carlo analysis. However, because this method is computationally expensive, new approaches with higher efficiency have been developed. Many popular methods are based on the surrogate models developed with Polynomial Chaos theory. However, size of these models can be prohibitively large for realistic examples. Hence, this paper provides a novel methodology to use an ensemble of weaker models to improve efficiency. Finally, a numerical example with a DDR4 topology is provided.

articleTitle: Improved Heating Uniformity of a 3-kWatt 2.45GHz Microwave Dryer Using Multiple Multi-Slotted Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: For improving heating uniformity we propose a 3-kWatt 2.45GHz microwave dryer using multiple multi-slotted waveguides with the horizontal and vertical array slots. Microwave source of each 2.45GHz magnetron is controlled to improve heating uniformity. The proposed dryer consists of two waveguide with the horizontal slots and one waveguide with the vertical slots. The input power was optimized for improved uniformity of temperature. The optimized power applied to each waveguide. Compared with the conventional microwave dryer, the proposed microwave dryer has improved the heating uniformity up to approximately 55%.

articleTitle: Hybrid-PIC Simulation of Nonlinear Wave-Particle Interactions in the Earth's Radiation Belts
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The Earth's magnetosphere is a complex plasma environment that is heavily influenced by the geomagnetic field. The particles in the near-Earth space environment can be classified into two major “cold” and “hot” plasma populations. The cold plasma is dense and can be modeled as a fluid with linear physics. However, the hot plasma drives nonlinear interactions and resonances with the waves. To model the physics of the system, we have developed a hybrid simulation which combines a fluid and Particle In Cell (PIC) simulation using the finite-difference time-domain method (FDTD) for broadband whistler wave interactions in the magnetosphere. In this work, we consider the nonlinear amplification of whistler mode waves injected into the radiation belts as well as the precipitation of hot plasma electrons interacting with the waves.

articleTitle: Determining the Dispersive Features of Nanophotonic Structures Based on Hybrid FEM/TMM Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Determining the dispersion relation of nanophotonic structures is one of the biggest challenges especially for nano-scale inhomogeneous structures where several efforts have been directed. Here, we present a technique that leverages the accuracy and simplicity of the combination of transfer matrix method (TMM) and finite element method (FEM). This hybrid technique allows us to find the spatial dispersion, coupling strength and nature of the generated modes.

articleTitle: Hybrid Integration Scheme for the Evaluation of Strongly Singular Integral Over Curvilinear Triangle Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of combining two well-known schemes (singularity subtraction and singularity cancellation) to evaluate strongly near-singular integrals with the singularity present in the MoM discretization of the Magnetic Field Integral Equations, (MFIE). First, a subtraction of a singularity is applied. The resulting integrand presents a singular term, which is canceled with an appropriate variable transformation. The aim is to achieve good efficiency for a medium-low accuracy range and be able to reach machine precision increasing the quadrature order.

articleTitle: Terahertz Modeling of 2D Electron Gas Systems Using Multiphysics Time-Domain Solvers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, we present a rigorous numerical method for multiphysics and multiscale modeling of 2D electron gas (2DEG) systems at terahertz frequencies. Notably, we use finite difference time domain method for evaluation of Maxwell's equations, while hydrodynamic equations for electron transport modeling. The presented computation tools are useful for variety of terahertz modeling problems that use phenomenological understanding and optimization of the 2D electronics in transistors and graphene-like systems.

articleTitle: FDTD Modelling of Optical Polarisation Rotation in a Charged Quantum Dot - Micropillar System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We employ a quantum master equations approach based on a full-wave Maxwell-pseudospin model to describe the polarisation dynamics of a negatively charged quantum dot embedded in a micropillar cavity upon an ultrashort optical excitation. The set of equations is solved self-consistently in the time domain by the Finite-Difference Time-Domain method (FDTD). We demonstrate numerically a giant optical polarisation rotation (~ ±π/2) of a resonant circularly polarised pulse in realistic dot-cavity geometries. The model allows for optimisation of the polarisation rotation angle for realisation of spin-photon entanglement and ultrafast polarisation switching on a chip.

articleTitle: Quantifying Subgridding Errors when Modeling Multiscale Structures with FDTD
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper discusses the growing subgridding errors in Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) analysis when applied on electrically large subgrids. FDTD simulations in 1D and 2D spaces are used with a 1:3 contrast ratio. Error levels are found to be linearly proportional to the subgrid's electrical dimension along the wave's propagation path. This linear growth suggests numerical phase error mismatch between coarse and fine grids as the subgridding error source.

articleTitle: Comparison of Extruded and Capstone Meshes for Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Meshes generation is often one of the most time-consuming and challenging aspects of performing an analysis of a radio-frequency (RF) design. New powerful tools are becoming available that simplify the mesh generation task. This paper introduces a new meshing tool - Capstone - to the community with comparison to an extruded mesh. The example presented is a coaxial line since it is readily meshed both by extrusion and using Capstone.

articleTitle: Solving Maxwell's Equations with a Generalized Dispersive Material Madel on Overset Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An efficient and high-order accurate time-domain (FDTD) scheme for solving Maxwell's equations in second-order form with a generalized dispersive material (GDM) model is described. The equations are discretized using finite-differences, and advanced in time with a single-stage, three-level, spacetime scheme which remains stable up to the usual explicit CFL-one restriction, as proven using mode analysis. Composite overlapping grids are used to treat complex geometries with boundary-conforming grids, and a high-order upwind dissipation is added to ensure robust and stable approximations on overlapping grids. Properties of the GDM model, which can represent arbitrary dispersive bahaviours, are analysed. Numerical results for some newly developed exact solutions confirm the accuracy and stability of the new scheme.

articleTitle: Linear Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis of the Time-Dependent Schrödinger Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a novel linear adjoint sensitivity analysis approach of the time-dependent Schrodinger equation. Regardless of the number of design parameters, the proposed approach estimates the sensitivities of a general objective function with respect to all the design parameters using only one extra system simulation. The efficiency of the approach is illustrated here through a numerical example.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Development of Negative Refraction
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Negative refraction in prisms built of periodic unit cells is a steady-state phenomenon that requires a finite amount time to develop. A signal transmitted through such a prism will initially be refracted positively. As time increases, the direction of refraction shifts toward the steady state angle of refraction. Signals that are shorter than the time required to reach steady state are not negatively refracted.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a 94GHz LTCC Integrated Horn Antenna Using High Impedance Periphery
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: There is a growing interest to implement antenna-in-package (AiP) systems for a variety of applications such as imaging, beamforming, integrated transceivers, and radars. Substrate integrated pyramidal antennas are valuable AiP candidates owing to their small form factor, integration ease, and high gain. However, height reduction, dielectric losses and integration of the latter can drastically degrade their gain pattern and limit their applications. This degradation is mainly due to undesired excitations on the surface of the dielectric. For the first time in this paper, we present a Grounded Co-Planar Waveguide-fed (GCPW) 94GHz low temperature cofired ceramic (LTCC) pyramidal horn antenna. To prevent parasitic TE excitations, a mushroom type High Impedance Surface (HIS) periphery is implemented. The combined antenna with HIS surrounding leads to approximately 2.3dB improvement in gain. Concurrently, the 3dB beamwidth is reduced by 26° in both E-Plane and H-Plane.

articleTitle: Data-Enabled Poisson Equation Solver Using Multiple Input Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs)
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We explore the possibility of using multiple input artificial neural networks for the solution of Poisson Equation. Results are shown for 1D case considering a boundary value problem with Dirichlet boundary conditions. As opposed to previous work, we consider the cases where input to the ANN is provided at multiple input nodes. A typical variation is considered containing sinc and cosine type functions and output validation is shown for different discretization steps. Time and error performances of the algorithm are presented.

articleTitle: EM-Driven Size Reduction of UWB MIMO Antennas with Feed Line Modifications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss an efficient size reduction technique for wideband MIMO antennas in a parallel configuration. Our approach exploits tapered feed lines of various complexities (from two to five sections), applied in order to improve antenna matching, thus creating a room for footprint reduction. Obtaining the minimum possible size while ensuring acceptable performance (especially, isolation |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>| ≤ -20 dB within the operating band) is secured by rigorous constrained EM-driven design optimization involving all geometry parameters of the antenna. Numerical results indicate that increasing the feed line complexity has a positive impact on antenna miniaturization.

articleTitle: On the Effect of Dissipation and Nonlocality on Unidirectional and Topological Surface Plasmon-Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Unidirectional surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) on nonreciprocal material platforms are currently the subject of significant interest. In this abstract, we revisit this exciting topic, discussing the role of the nonlocal response of a magnetized plasmonic material. Our analytical calculations and frequency-domain finite-element simulations confirm that a nonlocal correction in the material model implies the absence of purely unidirectional SPP modes below the plasma frequency. However, we also show that, depending on the considered configuration, the presence of even moderate levels of loss (absorption or radiation) can practically restore the unidirectionality of this mode. Our findings have important implications in the context of nonreciprocal and topological electromagnetic systems.

articleTitle: Material Models in Full-Wave Nonlinear Optics (invited)
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present advanced material models describing light-matter interaction for numerical simulation of nonlinear optical responses. We build the models on electron transport equations, carrier kinetics equations, and the effective dipole oscillator equation. Coupled to the Maxwell equations, they enable the study of nonlinear photonic elements such as nonlinear absorbers, optical modulators, and switches.

articleTitle: Design Guidelines for Magnetically Coupled Resonant Coils with Data Transfer Capability
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this contribution the authors investigate the possibility of improving the performances of a coupled Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) - Power Line Communications (PLC) system in case the WPT system is characterised by a four coils structure. The main idea is to use the so-called transmitting and receiving coil (the two “inner” coils) as access point for the PLC modems and use the drive and load loops (the two “outer” coils) as usual access point for power. The simulations results show that a higher wider band for communication is achieved with respect the previously proposed system.

articleTitle: An X-Band Oblique Polarized Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An X-band oblique polarized array is designed and manufactured, the scan range is positive negative 45deg. The antenna choose the printed dipole antenna. By using a short-circuited probe balun and adding a parasitic patch on the top of the dipole, the bandwidth of it is extended to be whole X-band. The antenna is improved to be double plates with two face radiation dipoles and a lot of metallization holes to close the balun radiation, which could reduce the difference between the horizontal polarization patterns and the vertical polarization patterns when wide-angle scan. The array is measured and the results show it can achieve X-band 45deg scan work.

articleTitle: Radiated Fields of Patch Antennas - A Comparison of Simulated and Analytic Results
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper compares the beamwidth of the fields radiated by a rectangular patch antenna using FEKO simulations and analytic formulations. Typical analytic estimates use over-simplified models that fail to account for the air-dielectric boundary. The analytic estimates in this work realize the radiated fields using Green's functions that presume filaments of magnetic current about the perimeter of the patch antenna. Accordingly, the formulation accounts for the air dielectric boundary as well as surface waves. The filaments of magnetic current are based on the cavity model operating at resonance. Comparisons are made to the approximations found in [1] as well as to simulations by the commercial software FEKO.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Wireless Systems for Simultaneous Power and Data Transfer
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Wireless systems that can simultaneously transmit power and data enable the development of battery-less and wire-free sensing for many important applications. In this work, recent advances on simultaneous Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) and wireless data communication are investigated. Moreover, a comparison of WPT methods based on inductive coupling, resonant inductive coupling, Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (SCMR), and Conformal SCMR (CSCMR) is presented.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Electrical Properties Tomography Using a Simplified Contrast-Source Inversion Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The contrast source inversion (CSI) method is a well-known inversion technique that has been utilized in a wide range of application areas. Here we show that in the specific situation of electrical properties tomography (EPT) in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which is a so-called hybrid inverse problem, since data is collected inside the reconstruction domain, the CSI method can be simplified to what is essentially a single forward simulation provided the electromagnetic field has an E-polarized field structure. As a consequence, the computational costs are significantly reduced and our experiments show that reconstructions obtained with the simplified CSI method have essentially the same accuracy as reconstructions obtained with the full CSI inversion method.

articleTitle: Dual-Band High Split Ratio Bagley Power Divider Based on Multi-T-Section Characterizaion of High Impedance Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We propose a dual-band 10:1:10 3-way Bagley power divider (BPD). The high characteristic impedance transmission lines in the conventional divider are replaced by dual-band T -shaped structures. To validate the design methodology, a prototype is designed to operate at 1 and 2 GHz. Simulation results show input port matching better than -20 dB, and transmission parameters, \pmbS21 (equals \pmbS41) and \pmbS31, around -4 dB and -14 dB, at the design frequencies, respectively.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Induction Sensing for Buried Explosive Hazards Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Detection and identification of subsurface improvised explosive devices (IED) remains one of the most pressing military and civilian problems worldwide. Usually, IED-s are made only with low conducting and/or no metallic parts and therefore are undetectable with conventional metal detectors and electromagnetic induction (EMI) sensors. To overcome this limitation and to fill the gap between the conventional EMI induction and radar sensing frequency bands, our group has developed a next generation High Frequency EMI (HFEMI) sensor, operating between 50 kHz and 15 MHz. Both numerical and in-lab experimental studies have showed that the new EMI sensor is able to detect high conducting (metals) as well as low conducting (carbon rods), low metal content (short wires) and nonconducting (voids in conducting soil) targets. For validating the system's detection capabilities under real world conditions, the system was deployed at an IED test site and EMI data were collected for a set of targets. In this paper, measured and numerical data are presented and analyzed for subsurface IEDs.

articleTitle: Polarization Transformations Based Metasurfaces for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents two different configurations of metasurfaces for 5G applications. The field transformations (polarization transformations) can be achieved using metasurfaces modelled through Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs). The configurations used in this paper are dielectric resonator and metallic metasurfaces that can be used to obtain quarter-wave transformations for an operating frequency range 28-33 GHz and 26-40 GHz respectively. The unit cell analysis for both types of metasurfaces using TE and TM polarization and phase difference between transmitted fields for both polarizations is maintained within 90° ± 20°.

articleTitle: Analysis of Freshwater Curved and Flat Spiral Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recent research shows that freshwater mussels are very effective as biological sensors for measuring pollutant levels in rivers. Electronic assembly mounted on top of mussel shells, or backpacks, measures the periodic opening and closing of the valves that is directly related to the nitrogen content of the water. These sensors communicate with a surface station through a radio operating at 300 MHz. Mussel backpacks require light-weight, small, broadband antennas with high efficiency in freshwater environment. Conventional spiral antennas satisfy these requirements but are ill-fitted to the curved shell surface. In this work, we design low-cost curved spiral antennas for mussel backpacks. Our numerical experiments with FEKO indicate relatively constant reflection coefficient of curved spiral antenna in freshwat<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">er</sup> at 300 MHz with values comparable with the flat spiral geometry.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Using Magneto-Electric Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system using Magneto- Electric Dipoles (MEDs) is proposed. These elements are based on the concept of the Huygens source and considered as complementary antennas combining electric and magnetic dipoles. This wireless power transfer system is able to achieve 0.58 GHz bandwidth from 1.83 to 2.41 GHz (27%), while maintaining a power transfer efficiency above 80% for a distance equal to 0.2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength at the central operating frequency). A maximum power transfer efficiency of 97% is obtained at 1.93 GHz and 2.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Numerical Mesh Truncation Boundary Conditions Optimized via Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Mesh truncation in Finite Element Method (FEM) is critical and presents conflicting options. Boundary Integral (BI) option yields very accurate results but results in non-sparse solution matrix while Artificial Absorbers (AAs) or Absorbing Boundary Conditions (ABCs) preserves sparsity of the matrix, they need to be placed sufficiently far away from the structure to yield accurate data, resulting in large number of unknowns. Paper presents a method to optimize the placement of the truncation boundary close to the object being modeled to minimize the size of the problem and the run time Optimization is object-dependent as it should be and is achieved using Machine Learning (ML). The proposed scheme is promising but needs further study to fully explore its potential to be of practical use.
